card.name: Yumsharol Jagoi
card.tagline: A Meitei folk dance from Manipur depicting house construction through hand gestures.
card.profile: Yumsharol Jagoi is a traditional dance form of the Meitei people from Manipur, India. It centers on the depiction of house construction through specialized hand gestures known as Yumsharol Khutthek. The dance is performed during the Lai Haraoba festival, which honors Meitei deities and the creation of the world. It serves as both a spiritual and artistic expression of community life and traditional skills.
card.insight: During the Lai Haraoba festival, dancers perform Yumsharol Jagoi, using specific hand gestures called Yumsharol Khutthek to mimic the physical stages of building a traditional Meitei house.
card.profile_long: Yumsharol Jagoi, also referred to as Yumsharon Jagoi, is a traditional dance form originating from the Meitei people of Manipur, India. It is recognized as a piece of Meitei intangible cultural heritage. The dance is defined by its focus on the physical process of building a house, which is communicated through a specific vocabulary of hand gestures known as Yumsharol Khutthek. These gestures, which translate to 'hand gestures of house construction,' represent the various steps involved in the architectural creation of a home. The performance is deeply embedded within the Lai Haraoba festival, a significant cultural event that celebrates the Meitei gods and the creation of the world according to Meitei religion and culture. The dance functions as both a spiritual and artistic medium, demonstrating respect for traditional ways of life and honoring the technical skills required for house building within Meitei civilization. The performance is accompanied by the Yumsharol song and the music of the pena, a traditional instrument. While the hand gestures are a documented component of the dance, other technical aspects such as specific footwork, body posture, and costume requirements are not described in sources.

claims.text: Yumsharol Jagoi is a traditional dance form of the Meitei people from Manipur, India.
The dance shows the process of building a house using special hand movements known as Yumsharol Khutthek.
The dance is performed along with the Yumsharol song and the music of a traditional instrument called the pena.
Yumsharol Jagoi is an important part of Lai Haraoba, a festival that celebrates the Meitei gods and the creation of the world.
The performance is both spiritual and artistic, showing respect for traditional ways of life and honoring the skills of house building as part of community life.
It is a Meitei intangible cultural heritage.
